answer: Use bonded sponsorship to stop clones. First, a newcomer enters only through one narrow inlet: an established agent stakes a $200 bond on it. Second, each sponsor may vouch for at most three newcomers per quarter, so no farm slips in through one account. Third, the newcomer works supervised for thirty days. If proven a clone, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses sponsorship for a year. Forging 10,000 clones needs 3,334 sponsors and $2,000,000 in bonds. Like an island where guests wander only after a resident vouches for them, trust enters through a known door.
